summary:
MarsHab — Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map
Team: TerrraNexis

MarsHab is an interactive Mars exploration and survival-planning platform developed to help future astronauts navigate and explore Jezero Crater using real NASA planetary data.

The platform combines digital elevation models, slope analysis, and A* pathfinding to generate three route strategies: shortest-distance, terrain-aware, and science-priority routes through a verified Perseverance rover observation site.

Beyond navigation, MarsHab evaluates mission feasibility, estimates resource requirements, and supports emergency-return planning and interactive mission simulations. Historical NASA MEDA observations, including temperature, atmospheric pressure, and wind measurements, provide additional environmental context.

MarsHab addresses the challenge by transforming complex planetary datasets into an accessible, interactive mission-planning experience. Its terrain visualization, route comparisons, and English–Myanmar interface help users understand the challenges of exploring Mars.

Our goal is to demonstrate how authentic space science data, geospatial analysis, and computational algorithms can support more informed exploration decisions while inspiring future scientists, engineers, and space explorers.
details:
MarsHab — Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map

Team: TerrraNexis

MarsHab is an interactive Mars exploration and survival-planning web application developed by Team TerrraNexis for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It helps future astronauts explore Martian terrain, plan routes, assess mission feasibility, and prepare for simulated emergencies using real NASA planetary data.

The application focuses on Jezero Crater and integrates digital elevation models, slope analysis, A* terrain-aware pathfinding, science waypoint navigation, historical environmental observations, and resource-budget estimation.

MarsHab provides three routing strategies: shortest-distance routing, terrain-aware routing, and science-priority routing through a verified Perseverance rover observation site. It also supports mission simulation, emergency-return planning, and mission reporting.

Developed using React, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, Three.js, QGIS, and GDAL, MarsHab combines scientific data with interactive visualization. Its English–Myanmar interface makes planetary exploration concepts accessible to a wider audience.

The project aims to demonstrate how real planetary datasets and computational methods can support informed exploration planning. MarsHab is an educational mission-planning prototype, not a certified astronaut navigation or life-support system.
